question: Fund totals from 990 narratives for the whole tail-CF frame: regex the Part III / Schedule O text of every FY2022-FY2024 990 of the 641 tail CFs (GivingTuesday mirror XML; robots.txt 404) for statements such as 'manages over N funds', 'endowment consists of approximately N individual funds' and 'N scholarship funds', and record the count, scope (all funds / endowed / one type) and qualifier ('over', 'approximately')
conclusion_affected: Rule F (opex x DAF funds / all funds) for tail CFs; whether DAF cost per account is understated by dollar-based rules A and G
rationale: Two of the 15 all-fund totals in the sample came from FY2024 990 narratives (Luzerne 'over 400 funds', NW Georgia 'over 200 charitable funds'), and three more 990s gave type or endowment counts. A 990 count has the same period as the Schedule D DAF count and opex, which website counters do not

question: OCR the image-only annual reports already located for sampled tail CFs (Parkersburg Area CF 2022-23 and 2023-24; Community Foundation for Loudoun and Northern Fauquier PDFs uploaded 2024-10 and 2025-06) and transcribe any fund counts by type; Loudoun's 2021 and 2022 text reports list counts for all seven types
conclusion_affected: Type mix (DAF vs designated, FOI, scholarship, agency, unrestricted) at tail CFs; currency of the Loudoun and Parkersburg denominators
rationale: Only one sampled CF (Loudoun, 2022) publishes counts for every fund type; its later reports and Parkersburg's last two reports returned no text from pdftotext, so the most recent counts could not be read

question: Per-site directory counters for structured tail-CF fund directories: write parsers (one marker per fund, type headings) for Kansas Rural Communities Foundation (about 150 entries), Oregon Trail CF, Two Rivers CF, Berrien CF and the Randolph County 2023 funds list, and re-check the Morton directory's DAF sections against its 17 Schedule D DAFs; record counts only
conclusion_affected: Size of the rule-F set (n = 15 of 60) and its <$1m band (n = 4)
rationale: Five sampled CFs publish a full fund directory but state no total; free-text layouts made a generic count unreliable, so they were left uncounted. Morton was countable (106 non-DAF funds by type) because each entry carries the same link text

question: Test fixed cost per fund: once at least 40 tail CFs have an all-funds total, regress log opex on log total funds and log total assets (and DAF share of funds) to estimate whether operating cost scales with fund count (rule F) or with dollars (rule A)
conclusion_affected: Choice of central allocation rule for tail DAF cost (A, G or F); the 'fixed cost per account' reading in b45n33-long-tail-operating-cost.md §2.1
rationale: Whole-org opex per fund is fairly flat across the 15 counted CFs (median $2,108) while per-dollar cost under F rises down the bands (median 193 / 329 / 326 bps). That is consistent with a per-fund fixed cost, but n = 15 with 8 lower-bound totals cannot separate the two

question: Fund counts for robots-blocked and unreachable sampled CFs from sources that allow access: for the 12 sampled CFs whose sites were robots-blocked (6: incl. Oklahoma City CF host for Lawton, Brookline, Brevard), bot-challenged (2) or unreachable (4), look for fund counts in their own 990 narratives (FY2022-24) and in audited statements on state charity registries whose robots.txt and terms allow automated access
conclusion_affected: Non-response bias in the rule-F set (counted CFs may publish counts because they are larger or better resourced)
rationale: 12 of 60 sampled CFs (20%) could not be read within the robots and terms rules, and 19 more publish no fund count; the counted set's rule-A median (194 bps) is close to the frame (205), but non-response is not random by construction
